reaction.episode: CORRECTION through the Nov 4 close — SPX 7,688.62, only 1.99% off its 120-day high and 5.03% above its 200-day average of $7,320.35, while SMH closed $504.27 in Zone 2 and NVDA $200.13 on the Zone 1 floor, VIX 16.61, HY OAS 3.32 calm, mechanical tally 2 of 4. Today's live tape is much worse — SPY $736.67 down 3.93%, QQQ $652.78 down 5.66%, VIX 26.73 intraday — and NVDA at $182.95 has slipped into Zone 2 intraday, but the episode state is close-based and no close has printed the zone breaks yet.
reaction.invalidation: The Probe stance is wrong if SMH closes below $470 and NVDA closes below $175 on expanding volume, or if VIX closes above 25 with HY OAS above 4% — either voids the zone thesis and turns the correction into a deeper drawdown regime. A held SPX close back above 7,820 with SMH reclaiming $580 would void the correction read the other way.

ladder.response: Hold the probe, do not average down into the break — the next zone down is the escalation, and sizing waits for a new zone print and a fresh tally.
ladder.trigger: SMH closes below $470 (Zone 2 floor) or NVDA closes below $175 (Zone 2 floor)

ladder.response: Probe fires on NVDA at Tranche A starter size — the only name inside its zone with a confirming print.
ladder.trigger: NVDA closes inside Zone 2 ($175-185) with the mechanical tally at 3 of 4 (volume climax or VIX rollover confirming)

ladder.response: Treat as the bull trap: do not chase, do not add on the bounce — wait for the failure-zone retest verdict and the second-low test before any further entry.
ladder.trigger: SPX bounces into the 7,750-7,820 failure zone, or SMH into 580-600, and stalls or fails

ladder.response: Stand down — no new probes, ladder void, regime-break conditions met; reassess from cash.
ladder.trigger: VIX closes above 25 or HY OAS closes above 4%

ladder.response: Regime break: the correction thesis is void, stance moves to Watch from cash until a new episode state prints.
ladder.trigger: SPX closes below its 200-day average of $7,320.35

reaction.trapRisk: Today's washout could print the first low near the S&P 500's 200-day average — but the first bounce off a washout low is the trap case in this tape: the Nov 4 session already showed the pattern, index up 1.58% while SMH fell 2.75%. Entries wait for the failure-zone retest verdict or a second low that holds, not for the first green day; the probe fires only on a confirmed Zone 2 close, never intraday.

strategyPosture: Probe, armed not fired. SMH closed in Zone 2 with credit calm and a 2-of-4 tally, and NVDA has slipped into Zone 2 intraday — but the capitulation confirmations are absent, the tape is still falling, and no close has printed a zone break. The probe fires only on a confirmed Zone 2 close, never intraday; no new entries, no averaging down into the break.

themes.counterRead: The rotation read holds while credit stays loose: the weakness is concentrated in the handful of names that dominate the index by weight, and the index is not confirming a broad rollover. But today the index itself is down 3.93% intraday with VIX at 26.73, up 60.93% on the day — the rotation read is under its hardest test, and if lending standards tighten or HY OAS breaks 4%, the rotation read fails and this becomes a rollover. The gap is the signal, not the noise.
themes.dataAnchor: SPX closed Nov 4 at 7,688.62, down 1.99% from its 120-day trailing high of 7,844.52; live today SPY is $736.67, down 3.93%, and QQQ $652.78, down 5.66%. themes.label: Rotation, Not Rollover
themes.narrative: The tape reads as a broad correction — AI names down 20-50% in a month — yet the index itself was only 1.99% off its 120-day high at the Nov 4 close. The market believes leadership is rotating, not that the market is breaking. Today's intraday washout is the first day the index itself has joined the drawdown in size.
themes.watchFor: HY OAS above 4% or SLOOS rising toward 40% voids the rotation read; SPX closing below its 200-day of 7,320.35 ends it outright.

themes.counterRead: Prices say the AI cycle is over; revenue says it is still compounding at 22-92%. The gap is the opportunity — but only 2 of 4 mechanical capitulation signals have confirmed (zone occupancy and credit calm), with no volume climax and no VIX rollover yet. And NVDA and PLTR carry ACUTE_CATALYST decline reasons, not pure sentiment, so the catalyst must be understood before sizing; multiple compression can persist while revenues grow, as AMAT shows with revenue up only 11.4% against a 55.8% drawdown. A zone print alone is not a bottom call; it is a probe condition, and the close decides it.

themes.label: AI Infrastructure: Revenues Up, Prices Down
themes.narrative: The AI bubble is bursting — semiconductors are in free fall, SMH is down 11.17% in five days and 19.32% in twenty at the Nov 4 close, and the complex is being abandoned. The midterm chip rout deepened the story: TSMC sank 10% and UMC 16% after the Democrats' midterm wins.
themes.watchFor: SMH close versus the $470 Zone 2 floor; NVDA close inside $175-185 completes the probe condition.

themes.counterRead: The election is a real catalyst, not pure sentiment — the Texas outcome changes the merchant-power math, and the price move may be repricing the model itself rather than overshooting it. But the magnitude, 42.5-53.9% off highs against 19-28% revenue growth plus insider buying at the VST trough, says the market has priced the vote as a structural hit before the Nov 6 report has printed. If that report confirms margin or regime damage, the overshoot read dies; if it holds, this is the screened trough to verify, not a chase.
themes.dataAnchor: VST is $113.17 live, down 42.5% from its 52-week high with RSI 29.4, down 6.04% today; VRT is $174.99, down 53.9% from its high with RSI 33.7, down 14.8% today. Against that, VST revenue is still growing 19.1% year over year, insiders bought $1.17M at the trough, and VRT revenue is growing 27.7% year over year. VST's Nov 6 report is flagged in the headlines as the item that has to settle the vote overhang.
themes.label: Merchant Power: The Texas Vote Is a Real Catalyst
themes.narrative: The US midterm election outcome killed the AI power trade — merchant power generators sold off as the market priced policy risk into the nuclear and power buildout, with Vistra falling 14% on the Texas election vote. The election event carries 39 matched headlines, the highest signal count in the input.
themes.watchFor: VST Nov 6 report — margins and guidance versus the vote overhang — decides whether this is a trough or a re-rating.

themes.counterRead: Rates and credit agree the stress is equity-concentrated, not systemic — the bond market is not pricing a credit event. But credit is a lagging confirmer, and VIX is 26.73 intraday, already above the 25 stand-down line: the calm read survives only until the close. The Dec 8-9 FOMC is the dated test of that calm — a hawkish surprise is the path by which calm credit flips.
themes.dataAnchor: The 10-year is 4.95% and the 2-year 4.61%, with the 2s10s curve at +0.34 — not inverted. HY OAS is 3.32, calm and below the 4% stand-down line. themes.label: Credit Refuses to Confirm the Panic
themes.narrative: Hot data means more hikes — the Dec 8-9 FOMC is flagged HIGH signal strength and the market is pricing the Fed signaling higher rates. A 5.66% QQQ down day with VIX up 61% reads as a funding-stress event.
themes.watchFor: VIX closing above 25 or HY OAS above 4% breaks the calm read; the Dec 8-9 FOMC is the dated test.
